baseline.answer:
### Balanced Comparison of YOLO and RT-DETR on Real-Time Object Detection

#### Similarities

Both YOLO and RT-DETR are designed to address the challenges of real-time object detection, aiming to balance speed and accuracy for practical deployment in applications such as autonomous driving and video surveillance. They both represent end-to-end trainable frameworks that unify the detection pipeline into a single model, eliminating the need for multi-stage processing typical in earlier systems like R-CNN variants.

- **Unified Architecture**: YOLO frames object detection as a single regression problem, predicting bounding boxes and class probabilities directly from full images in one evaluation. This unified architecture allows for end-to-end optimization on detection performance.  
  > *"We present YOLO, a new approach to object detection. Prior work on object detection repurposes classifiers to perform detection. Instead, we frame object detection as a regression problem to spatially separated bounding boxes and associated class probabilities. A single neural network predicts bounding boxes and class probabilities directly from full images in one evaluation. Since the whole detection pipeline is a single network, it can be optimized end-to-end directly on detection performance."* (YOLO, Abstract)

- **Real-Time Focus**: Both models emphasize real-time inference capabilities. YOLO achieves real-time speeds of up to 155 FPS with its Fast YOLO variant, while RT-DETR is explicitly designed as the first real-time end-to-end Transformer-based detector, achieving 108 FPS on a T4 GPU.  
  > *"Fast YOLO is the fastest general-purpose object detector in the literature and YOLO pushes the state-of-the-art in real-time object detection."* (YOLO, Conclusion)

#### Differences

The core architectural and methodological differences between YOLO and RT-DETR stem from their underlying models—YOLO uses CNN-based single-shot detection, while RT-DETR leverages Transformer-based end-to-end detection without Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS).

- **Detection Mechanism and NMS Dependency**:
  - YOLO relies on a grid-based prediction system where each grid cell predicts multiple bounding boxes and class probabilities, followed by NMS to filter overlapping detections. This introduces post-processing latency and hyperparameter sensitivity.
  - RT-DETR eliminates NMS entirely by using a set-based global reasoning approach via Transformers, which improves inference stability and reduces dependency on post-processing thresholds.
    > *"The YOLO series has become the most popular framework for real-time object detection due to its reasonable trade-off between speed and accuracy. However, we observe that the speed and accuracy of YOLOs are negatively affected by the NMS. Recently, end-to-end Transformer-based detectors (DETRs) have provided an alternative to eliminating NMS."* (RT-DETR, Abstract)

- **Architecture and Speed-Accuracy Trade-off**:
  - YOLO uses a single CNN backbone with spatial grid predictions, enabling very fast inference but suffering from localization errors.
  - RT-DETR introduces an efficient hybrid encoder that decouples intra-scale interaction and cross-scale fusion, improving both speed and accuracy. It also supports flexible speed tuning by adjusting decoder layers without retraining.
    > *"RT-DETR includes two key enhancements: an efficient hybrid encoder that expeditiously processes multi-scale features, and the uncertainty-minimal query selection that improves the quality of initial object queries."* (RT-DETR, Conclusion)

- **Performance and Generalization**:
  - YOLO generalizes well to new domains (e.g., artwork) due to its simple, unified structure.
  - RT-DETR outperforms YOLO in both accuracy (53.1% AP vs. prior YOLOs) and speed (108 FPS), while also surpassing other DETR variants significantly in efficiency.
    > *"RT-DETR-R50 / R101 achieves 53.1% / 54.3% AP on COCO and 108 / 74 FPS on T4 GPU, outperforming previously advanced YOLOs in both speed and accuracy."* (RT-DETR, Abstract)

#### Summary

| Aspect | YOLO | RT-DETR |
|-------|------|--------|
| **Architecture** | CNN-based, single-shot, grid prediction | Transformer-based, end-to-end, no NMS |
| **Speed** | Up to 155 FPS (Fast YOLO) | Up to 108 FPS (RT-DETR-R50) |
| **Accuracy (AP)** | Lower than RT-DETR on COCO | 53.1% AP (R50), outperforms YOLO |
| **Post-processing** | Requires NMS | Eliminates NMS via set prediction |
| **Flexibility** | Fixed pipeline | Adjustable decoder depth for speed tuning |
| **Generalization** | Strong on non

## Abstract

We present YOLO, a new approach to object detection. Prior work on object detection repurposes classifiers to perform detection. Instead, we frame object detection as a regression problem to spatially separated bounding boxes and associated class probabilities. A single neural network predicts bounding boxes and class probabilities directly from full images in one evaluation. Since the whole detection pipeline is a single network, it can be optimized end-to-end directly on detection performance.

Our unified architecture is extremely fast. Our base YOLO model processes images in real-time at 45 frames per second. A smaller version of the network, Fast YOLO, processes an astounding 155 frames per second while still achieving double the mAP of other real-time detectors. Compared

## 6. Conclusion

We introduce YOLO, a unified model for object detection. Our model is simple to construct and can be trained directly on full images. Unlike classifier-based approaches, YOLO is trained on a loss function that directly corresponds to detection performance and the entire model is trained jointly.

Fast YOLO is the fastest general-purpose object detector in the literature and YOLO pushes the state-of-the-art in real-time object detection. YOLO also generalizes well to new domains making it ideal for applications that rely on fast, robust object detection.

Acknowledgements: This work is partially supported by ONR N00014-13-1-0720, NSF IIS-1338054, and The Allen Distinguished Investigator Award.

baseline.answer:
### Balanced Comparison of YOLO and RT-DETR on Real-Time Object Detection

#### Similarities

Both YOLO and RT-DETR are designed to address the challenges of real-time object detection, aiming to balance speed and accuracy for practical deployment in applications such as autonomous driving and video surveillance. They both represent end-to-end trainable frameworks that unify the detection pipeline into a single model, eliminating the need for multi-stage processing typical in earlier systems like R-CNN variants.

- **Unified Architecture**: YOLO frames object detection as a single regression problem, predicting bounding boxes and class probabilities directly from full images in one evaluation. This unified architecture allows for end-to-end optimization on detection performance.  
  > *"We present YOLO, a new approach to object detection. Prior work on object detection repurposes classifiers to perform detection. Instead, we frame object detection as a regression problem to spatially separated bounding boxes and associated class probabilities. A single neural network predicts bounding boxes and class probabilities directly from full images in one evaluation. Since the whole detection pipeline is a single network, it can be optimized end-to-end directly on detection performance."* (YOLO, Abstract)

- **Real-Time Focus**: Both models emphasize real-time inference capabilities. YOLO achieves real-time speeds of up to 155 FPS with its Fast YOLO variant, while RT-DETR is explicitly designed as the first real-time end-to-end Transformer-based detector, achieving 108 FPS on a T4 GPU.  
  > *"Fast YOLO is the fastest general-purpose object detector in the literature and YOLO pushes the state-of-the-art in real-time object detection."* (YOLO, Conclusion)

#### Differences

The core architectural and methodological differences between YOLO and RT-DETR stem from their underlying models—YOLO uses CNN-based single-shot detection, while RT-DETR leverages Transformer-based end-to-end detection without Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS).

- **Detection Mechanism and NMS Dependency**:
  - YOLO relies on a grid-based prediction system where each grid cell predicts multiple bounding boxes and class probabilities, followed by NMS to filter overlapping detections. This introduces post-processing latency and hyperparameter sensitivity.
  - RT-DETR eliminates NMS entirely by using a set-based global reasoning approach via Transformers, which improves inference stability and reduces dependency on post-processing thresholds.
    > *"The YOLO series has become the most popular framework for real-time object detection due to its reasonable trade-off between speed and accuracy. However, we observe that the speed and accuracy of YOLOs are negatively affected by the NMS. Recently, end-to-end Transformer-based detectors (DETRs) have provided an alternative to eliminating NMS."* (RT-DETR, Abstract)

- **Architecture and Speed-Accuracy Trade-off**:
  - YOLO uses a single CNN backbone with spatial grid predictions, enabling very fast inference but suffering from localization errors.
  - RT-DETR introduces an efficient hybrid encoder that decouples intra-scale interaction and cross-scale fusion, improving both speed and accuracy. It also supports flexible speed tuning by adjusting decoder layers without retraining.
    > *"RT-DETR includes two key enhancements: an efficient hybrid encoder that expeditiously processes multi-scale features, and the uncertainty-minimal query selection that improves the quality of initial object queries."* (RT-DETR, Conclusion)

- **Performance and Generalization**:
  - YOLO generalizes well to new domains (e.g., artwork) due to its simple, unified structure.
  - RT-DETR outperforms YOLO in both accuracy (53.1% AP vs. prior YOLOs) and speed (108 FPS), while also surpassing other DETR variants significantly in efficiency.
    > *"RT-DETR-R50 / R101 achieves 53.1% / 54.3% AP on COCO and 108 / 74 FPS on T4 GPU, outperforming previously advanced YOLOs in both speed and accuracy."* (RT-DETR, Abstract)

#### Summary

| Aspect | YOLO | RT-DETR |
|-------|------|--------|
| **Architecture** | CNN-based, single-shot, grid prediction | Transformer-based, end-to-end, no NMS |
| **Speed** | Up to 155 FPS (Fast YOLO) | Up to 108 FPS (RT-DETR-R50) |
| **Accuracy (AP)** | Lower than RT-DETR on COCO | 53.1% AP (R50), outperforms YOLO |
| **Post-processing** | Requires NMS | Eliminates NMS via set prediction |
| **Flexibility** | Fixed pipeline | Adjustable decoder depth for speed tuning |
| **Generalization** | Strong on non

We present YOLO, a new approach to object detection. Prior work on object detection repurposes classifiers to perform detection. Instead, we frame object detection as a regression problem to spatially separated bounding boxes and associated class probabilities. A single neural network predicts bounding boxes and class probabilities directly from full images in one evaluation. Since the whole detection pipeline is a single network, it can be optimized end-to-end directly on detection performance.

Our unified architecture is extremely fast. Our base YOLO model processes images in real-time at 45 frames per second. A smaller version of the network, Fast YOLO, processes an astounding 155 frames per second while still achieving double the mAP of other real-time detectors. Compared

## 6. Conclusion

We introduce YOLO, a unified model for object detection. Our model is simple to construct and can be trained directly on full images. Unlike classifier-based approaches, YOLO is trained on a loss function that directly corresponds to detection performance and the entire model is trained jointly.

Fast YOLO is the fastest general-purpose object detector in the literature and YOLO pushes the state-of-the-art in real-time object detection. YOLO also generalizes well to new domains making it ideal for applications that rely on fast, robust object detection.
